newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia govt sees 97 GDP growth helped by industry.
newsitem.headline: Croatia govt sees 97 GDP growth helped by industry.

text.p: The Croatian government said on Tuesday it expected economic growth in 1997 to exceed seven percent thanks to a steady rise in industrial output and growth in tourism and other sectors.
Its new forecast more or less echoed recent remarks by Prime Minister Zlatko Matesa who saw gross domestic product (GDP) rising 7-8 percent this year.

Industrial output dipped 1.4 percent in July from June, but was still 8.0 percent higher compared with July 1996, according to the latest statistics. The January-July output rise was put at 5.2 percent year-on-year.

"This is long-term growth, as illustrated by a 22-month uninterrupted rise of the trend cycle. If this trend continues, industrial output will be six percent higher in 1997 than in 1996," the government said in a statement faxed to Reuters.
"With the evident growth in other sectors (tourism, construction, transports, agriculture) a gross domestic product growth exceeding 7.0 percent can be expected in 1997," the statement said.
Manufacturing makes up some 25 percent of GDP and tourism and agriculture contribute around 20 percent. Industry figures also include output of the mining and power industries.
But despite a dynamic production rise so far this year and strong domestic and export demand, independent economists expect a more modest GDP growth of around five percent.
After optimistic government forecasts for 1996, official statistics showed GDP had risen only 4.2 percent in real terms. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb newsroom +385 1 455 7075
